content.text:
Bug replicated and root-caused. Here's the full picture.

## What I saw in the browser

The dashboard loads fine and the catalog works, but the **Integration Flow** tab shows *"No declared topology for this system. Make sure its system host supports the graph verb, then refresh."* — for every selectable system. Notably, the system dropdown offers "domains / test", "Workspace", and a single **"orders / order-flow" with 4 components**, even though the workspace contains two separate systems (`domains/orders/fulfillment` and `domains/orders/order-flow`) with 2 components each.

The APIs are actually healthy: `/api/flow` returns all 6 integrations and `/api/topology` returns both system topologies (paths `domains/orders/fulfillment` and `domains/orders/order-flow`). No console errors, no failed requests. The failure is pure matching logic in the frontend.

## Root cause

Both system hosts declare the same system name — `domains/orders/fulfillment/order-flow/.intropy/scaffold.json` and `domains/orders/order-flow/order-flow/.intropy/scaffold.json` both record `name: order-flow` (fulfillment looks like a copy of order-flow that kept its host name). Both sit under the same `orders` parent folder, so:

1. The server (`summarize` in `internal/dashboard/handlers.go:205`) gives all four blocks `system: "order-flow"`, `domain: "orders"`.
2. The frontend groups by that name pair — `systemKey()` in `web/src/components/FlowView.tsx:131` returns `"orders/order-flow"` for all four, merging two distinct systems into one dropdown entry.
3. `topologyFor()` (`FlowView.tsx:142`) then looks for a single topology whose path contains **every** integration in the merged group. Neither `domains/orders/fulfillment` nor `domains/orders/order-flow` covers all four, so it returns `undefined` and the empty state renders.

That's why it only breaks from the repo root: run from inside one system directory, only that system's blocks are scanned, the group has 2 items, and its topology matches. The `systemKey` comment even says the domain/system pair exists so "two different domains that reuse a system name stay distinct" — but it doesn't protect against the same name reused *within* one domain. (Side effect of the same heuristic: `hello-world` shows up as "domains / test" because the top-level `domains` folder is mistaken for a domain.)

## Suggested fix

Key system identity by the system's root **directory** rather than its declared name: have the server include the host's directory (e.g. `systemPath: "domains/orders/fulfillment"`) on each summary, group on that in `FlowView`, and keep the declared name purely as the label (disambiguated with the path when two systems share a name). `topologyFor` then becomes a direct `topology.path === systemPath` lookup instead of the all-items prefix scan.

Want me to implement that?

      uid=6_100 StaticText "# OrderExtractor

.NET extractor integration. One run = one sweep: the runner lists the local
inbound folder, runs each swept JSON order through the Intropy extractor
pipeline, publishes the result as a CloudEvent to the `order` topic on
the in-memory Dapr pub/sub, deletes the source file, and exits. Scheduling
lives outside the block — the system host locally, a Kubernetes CronJob in
production.

## Run

```bash
task run
```

This seeds `./local/storage/order-extractor-source` with the bundled sample order, starts the
local stack (grafana/otel-lgtm observability plus the Intropy Idempotency Service
and Business Incident Service — see `local/platform-services/`), and runs the app
once under Dapr. You should see:

```
== APP == info: OrderExtractor.Pipeline[0]
== APP ==       Swept 1 file(s) from inbound
== APP == info: OrderExtractor.Pipeline[0]
== APP ==       Published ORD-1001 to topic order (pubsub)
```

The job exits by itself once the sweep completes (exit code 1 means at least
one file failed and was left in place). Confirm the source file is gone:

```bash
ls local/storage/order-extractor-source/
```

The message went into the extractor's own in-memory pub/sub — nothing
subscribes there. A standalone run verifies the extractor's whole job (sweep,
publish, clean up) without needing a consumer to exist.

Run `task run` a second time — it re-seeds the same order — and the pipeline
cancels at the idempotency check instead of publishing twice: the trace shows
the check step cancelled and no downstream steps.

Other tasks: `task build`, `task test`, `task clean` (remove `./local/storage`),
and `task services:down` (stop the local stack). See `Taskfile.yml`.

## Shared contracts

The canonical contract types (`Order`, `OrderLine`) live in the sibling
`../Contracts` project, referenced from `src/OrderExtractor.csproj`. It was
scaffolded together with this project (or already existed — components in the
same parent directory share it); the consuming loader deserializes exactly
those records.

## Container image

```bash
docker build --build-context contracts=../Contracts -t order-extractor .
```

Multi-stage build on the .NET 10 chiseled runtime. The shared contracts sibling
enters the build as the `contracts` named context (it lies outside this build
context). The image contains only the app — the Dapr sidecar and components
come from the deployment environment.

## Pipeline

Per swept file (`src/ExtractorRunner.cs` drives this once per run):

1. `Deserializer` parses the JSON into `In` and stamps `order_id` into the
   pipeline context.
2. `Validator` enforces required fields and basic business rules; failures are
   routed to the Business Incident Service.
3. Idempotency check — asks the Idempotency Service whether this `OrderId` /
   `OrderDate` combination was already processed; duplicates cancel the run.
4. `Transformer` maps `In` → the canonical `Order` shape from the shared
   contracts project (`../Contracts`) that the consuming loader deserializes.
5. `Serializer` wraps `Order` in a CloudEvent with `Subject` = order id and
   `Time` = order date.
6. The Dapr topic publisher sets the envelope source/type and sends it to
   `pubsub` / `order`.

On success (or an idempotent duplicate) the source file is deleted; a failed
file stays in the inbound folder and is retried on the next scheduled run,
which the run's exit code 1 asks the scheduler to record.
"

Fix implemented, verified in the browser, and your dashboard on port 8730 is now running the patched binary. Both order systems render their flows correctly — the screenshot above shows `domains/orders/order-flow` with its SFTP connector drawn as external, while the fulfillment system separately shows its file connector as disk.

## What changed

The root cause was system identity being keyed by declared name, so I introduced a path-based key end to end:

- `internal/dashboard/handlers.go` — each integration summary now carries `systemPath`, the root-relative directory of its system (`.` when the system is rooted at the workspace). Unlike the `system` name, it's unique, and it equals the `path` of the topology record the system's host emits.
- `web/src/components/FlowView.tsx` — `systemKey` groups by `systemPath` instead of the `domain/system` name pair, and `topologyFor` became an exact `topology.path === systemPath` lookup, replacing the "one record must cover every integration in the group" scan that returned nothing for the merged group. When two systems declare the same name, the dropdown qualifies the labels: "order-flow (domains/orders/fulfillment)" vs "order-flow (domains/orders/order-flow)".
- `web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx` — the catalog tree keys groups by `systemPath` too, so the sidebar now shows "fulfillment 2" and "order-flow 2" under orders instead of one merged "order-flow 4"; duplicate sibling names fall back to the folder name.
- Tests: extended the tree-coordinate and system-host tests to assert `systemPath`, and added `TestIntegrationsSystemPathDistinct` pinning this regression (two hosts declaring the same system name must keep distinct keys). `go test ./...` and the frontend build both pass.

## One thing you should know

The dashboard you had running was built from `feat/taskfile-graph-contract` (v0.8.0-72-g88fbcfcc — it had a "Test" nav tab). This checkout is `feature/v-next` at v0.8.0-59, so the restarted dashboard is missing those 13 commits. The fix lives in the `feature/v-next` working tree; if you're actively working on the other branch you'll want to bring it over there too.

This is a good commit point: the change is self-contained (server field + two frontend consumers + regression test), everything green. Want me to commit it on `feature/v-next`?
